orientation_convention:
Canonical hold for all downstream enclosure work — component face toward the viewer, USB edge at the top:
- Top edge ("head") = v = 0: J1 micro-B USB receptacle, mouth facing out of this edge, dead-centered at u ≈ 26.68 (span 21.951–31.4); cable enters perpendicular to this wall, insertion along +v [citation: parts table J1 row; README "micro-B USB"; outline center 26.67 in geometry summary].
- Left edge = u = 0: J3, 2×18 vertical header, v-span 4.23–49.11 [citation: parts table J3 row]. Right edge = u = 53.34: J4, 2×18 vertical header, identical v-span [citation: parts table J4 row]. The two flank headers define the board's working axis along v even though the outline is square.
- Bottom edge = v = 53.34: no connectors, plain edge [citation: absence of any part row spanning that edge in the parts table].
- User-facing face: the populated face carrying J1–J4 and U1 (parts 3.35–8.5 mm proud of it) [citation: parts table h column — extraction frame; not stated in README prose].
- In this view: USB top-center; J2 2-pin header ~3 mm LEFT of the centerline (u-center 23.62), ~10 mm below the top edge (v-center 10.16); regulator U1 right of centerline (u-center 35.05), ~17 mm below the top edge [citation: parts table J2/U1 rows + outline in geometry summary]. Left/right are NOT interchangeable: a mirrored design (J2 right of center) is wrong even if all booleans pass.
- Explicit limits: the README names no "up" direction; the v=0 head-edge is pinned by connector placement, the only orientation-defining feature present. Mounting holes must never be used to infer orientation on this board — they are fully rotation/mirror symmetric [citation: hole coordinates in geometry summary; README excerpt].
- Upright-vs-sideways handedness (USB-top vs USB-left in the user's hand) is not documented anywhere in the provided sources; what documentation does pin is edge-relative: USB opening on the v=0 wall centered at u = 26.68, header clearance on the u=0 and u=53.34 walls [citation: parts table J1/J3/J4 rows].
user_facing_features:
1. USB micro-B cable opening (J1) — the primary user-facing feature. On the v=0 wall (top wall in convention), centered at u = 26.68 (receptacle span u 21.951–31.4); shell 3.35 mm tall on the component face, mouth ~1.96 mm in from the board edge; cable approaches horizontally, perpendicular to the wall. An opening centered on any other wall, or off-center, is a semantic regression that boolean checks will not catch on this square board [citation: parts table J1 row; README "micro-B USB"].
2. GPIO header clearance (J3 left, J4 right) — two 2×18 vertical headers, 8.5 mm tall above the user face, spanning v 4.23–49.11 along both flanking edges. Users probe/jumper these pins: enclosure walls over the u=0 and u=53.34 flanks must be slotted/open over that v-span, or the design must be a carrier leaving the flanks exposed [citation: parts table J3/J4 rows].
3. Auxiliary 2-pin header (J2) — on the user face at center (23.62, 10.16): ~3 mm left of the board centerline, ~10 mm below the top edge, 8.5 mm tall. Function is undocumented in the README excerpt; treat as potentially user-reachable (unverified power/serial guess) and keep it accessible unless its function is confirmed safe to cover [citation: parts table J2 row; README excerpt — silent on J2].
4. Windows / button / indicator cutouts: NONE. README says "dev board, no display," and the parts table contains no display, button, or LED part. Any window or indicator opening in an enclosure for this board is invented, not user-facing [citation: README excerpt; parts table absence].
5. Support fact (not user-facing): 4 mounting holes, 2.7 mm drill, at (12.7, 5.457), (12.7, 47.883), (40.64, 5.457), (40.64, 47.883) — for standoffs only; symmetric under rotation and mirror, so they must not be treated as orientation evidence [citation: mounting-hole coordinates in geometry summary].
reasoning:
Source inventory: this step received exactly two anchors — (a) the README prose excerpt and (b) the extracted geometry summary (outline, mounting holes, per-part u/v spans + heights). The board repo itself (github.com/PartialScience/Custom-RP2040-Dev-Board, per experiments/runs/2026-10-10-rp2040-harness-v0.json) is not checked out locally, and the README excerpt arrived without an in-repo path, so every citation below anchors to these two board_context sources. I do not invent file paths I have not seen.
Derivation:
1. The README states no explicit orientation in prose ("minimal RP2040 board… dev board, no display") [citation: README excerpt in board_context]. Therefore the orientation must be pinned by the one human-interface part, corroborated by prose.
2. J1, footprint ZX62DB5PA830 (micro-B USB receptacle), is confirmed as the USB port by the README's "micro-B USB" [citation: parts table J1 row; README excerpt]. Its u-span [21.951, 31.4] centers at u = 26.68 vs board center 26.67 (Δ < 0.01 mm — dead-centered), and its v-span [1.963, 6.937] starts 1.96 mm from the v=0 edge [citation: parts table J1 row + outline in geometry summary]. A receptacle hugging one centered edge means the cable mates from the v=0 edge, plug axis parallel to the board plane, insertion direction +v. That edge is the board's "head."
3. Square-board hazard check (lesson-6 class): outline is 53.34×53.34 (square); mounting holes at u∈{12.7,40.64}, v∈{5.457,47.883} are exactly invariant under 180° rotation and both mirror axes; J3/J4 are an exact mirror pair (53.34−5.93 = 47.41, 53.34−1.69 = 51.65) [citation: geometry summary holes/outline + parts table J3/J4 rows]. So outline and holes carry ZERO orientation information. Only the connector cluster breaks symmetry: J1 (v≈0 position), J2 (u-center 23.62, left of centerline), U1 (u-center 35.05, right of centerline) [citation: parts table J1/J2/U1 rows]. Consequence: an enclosure opening rotated 90°, or a design mirrored (e.g., modeled looking from the solder side), passes every boolean clearance check on this board — the exact portrait-window failure mode. Hence the convention below is pinned explicitly.
4. Face assignment: all five listed parts sit on one face with heights 3.35–8.5 mm; the vertical through-hole headers stand 8.5 mm proud [citation: parts table h column]. That populated face is the user-facing (component) face; the opposite face is bare. Whether the extractor calls it +z or −z is a frame convention from the extraction, not from prose docs — flagged, not asserted from the README.
5. No display, no buttons, no LEDs appear in the README or the parts table [citation: README excerpt; parts table]. The entire user surface is: USB cable opening + GPIO/aux header access. Any window is unsupported by documentation.
